Linux · Rust · TypeScript

Meridian

A Linux desktop shell with a configurable dock, an app launcher, notifications, and settings for displays, storage, and other hardware.

Engineering choices and results

I built Meridian to bring desktop controls into one shell. Rust handles system integration, with a TypeScript interface for the dock, launcher, and settings. I used UDisks2 for storage controls and added display hot-plug handling with rollback. Compatibility depends on the available hardware and Wayland compositor protocols.

macOS · USB HCI · SwiftUI

Raw Bluetooth

An experimental userspace driver that uses an external USB Bluetooth adapter and Google Bumble to connect keyboards and mice to macOS. A SwiftUI app handles scanning, pairing, and saved devices.

Why I built it

I wanted to use Bluetooth keyboards and mice with an external USB adapter through a dedicated macOS app.

How input reaches macOS

  1. The app talks to the external adapter over USB HCI.
  2. Google Bumble discovers and pairs Bluetooth Low Energy devices.
  3. The driver decodes HID reports and forwards keyboard and mouse events to macOS.

Test setup

I tested a CSR USB adapter (0a12:0001), a Logitech M196 mouse, and a Logitech K250 keyboard on Intel macOS. Keyboard and mouse input worked on that setup. Audio remains experimental, and compatibility depends on the adapter and peripherals.

Wribate

Problem and contribution

During my internship at Innorize, I helped build a responsive web application for online debate and discussion. I worked on the frontend and REST APIs.

Engineering choices and results

I used Tailwind for the interface, MongoDB for persistence, and JWT authentication for the APIs. Caching and lazy loading improved load speed by about 30% in the project measurements. The résumé figure describes the changes measured during the internship and can vary by page and network.
